sentences.en: My fellow Americans, Memorial Day is a day of ceremonies and speeches.
sentences.zh: 各位美国同胞，阵亡将士纪念日是一个充满仪式和演讲的日子。

sentences.en: Throughout America today, we honor the dead of our wars.
sentences.zh: 今天，全美各地都在缅怀我们战争中的逝者。

sentences.en: Whatever you think about Ronald Reagan, they called him the great communicator for a reason.
sentences.zh: 无论你如何看待罗纳德·里根，人们称他为“伟大的沟通者”是有原因的。

sentences.en: The unknown soldier who has returned to us today and whom we lay to rest is symbolic of all our missing sons.
sentences.zh: 今天回到我们身边并安息的这位无名战士，象征着我们所有失踪的子弟。

sentences.en: This is him in 1984 during a military funeral at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery.
sentences.zh: 这是1984年他在阿灵顿国家公墓无名战士墓前举行军事葬礼时的情景。

sentences.en: On that Memorial Day, Reagan was eulogizing the remains of an unidentified service member from the Vietnam War.
sentences.zh: 在那个阵亡将士纪念日，里根正在为越战中一名身份不明的军人遗骸致悼词。

sentences.en: The remains would be entombed alongside three other unknown service members from World War I and II and the Korean War.
sentences.zh: 这具遗骸将与来自一战、二战和朝鲜战争的其他三位无名军人一起被安葬。
那是我们的乔·罗森伯格。

sentences.en: A horse-drawn carriage brought the casket to the tomb.
sentences.zh: 一辆马车将灵柩运送到了墓地。

sentences.en: It passed 250,000 onlookers, including hundreds of veterans who emerged out of the crowd to walk behind the remains on their way to Arlington.
sentences.zh: 灵柩经过了25万名围观者，其中包括数百名从人群中走出来，跟随灵柩前往阿灵顿的退伍军人。

sentences.en: The most powerful part, though, is when Reagan talks about who this unknown soldier might have been.
sentences.zh: 然而，最震撼的部分是里根谈到这位无名战士可能是什么样的人时。

sentences.en: Did he play on some street in a great American city?
sentences.zh: 他是否曾在某个美国大城市的街道上玩耍？

sentences.en: Or did he work beside his father on a farm out in America's heartland?
sentences.zh: 还是曾在美国腹地的农场里与父亲并肩劳作？

sentences.en: Did he look expectantly to return to a bride?
sentences.zh: 他是否满怀期待地盼望着回到新娘身边？

sentences.en: We'll never know the answers to these questions about his life.
sentences.zh: 关于他的人生，我们永远无法得知这些问题的答案。

sentences.en: As Reagan spoke, etched on the side of the tomb itself were the words,
sentences.zh: 当里根讲话时，墓碑侧面刻着这样的话：

sentences.en: It's all really moving, even knowing what we know now.
sentences.zh: 这一切真的很感人，即使我们现在已经知道了真相。

sentences.en: Which is that, although the person being buried that day might have been unknown to the public,
sentences.zh: 那就是，尽管那天被安葬的人在公众眼中可能是无名的，

sentences.en: a lot about his identity actually was known.
sentences.zh: 但关于他的身份，其实有很多信息是已知的。

sentences.en: The government likely even knew that he had a family who would like to have his body back.
sentences.zh: 政府甚至很可能知道他有家人希望能找回他的遗体。

sentences.en: How to honor unidentified remains has always been one of the great conundrums of war.
sentences.zh: 如何纪念身份不明的遗骸，一直是战争中最大的难题之一。

sentences.en: The Romans were fond of honoring them with an empty sarcophagus.
sentences.zh: 罗马人喜欢用空石棺来纪念他们。

sentences.en: After the Civil War, the Union buried 2,111 soldiers in a mass grave in Arlington
